selection_log.reason: Scale is always walked at Session 0.
Repository shape is always walked; this validation fixture is a minor surface of EOS with no independent handover.
Injection defence is an always-walk floor for agent runs, and this fixture has no validated deterministic monitor.
Agents may commit to a GitHub-backed repository, so staged and push-path protection are both required before credential-bearing use.
The committed fixture may outlive a quarter, so it needs a declared entry bar even though it holds no sensitive data.
The seed declares a manual, unvalidated guard adapter, so consequential actions must fall closed to manual execution.
requires_independent_deployability is true for one owned boundary.

rulings.reason: One operator and one small venture do not require ORG machinery.

rulings.decision: Keep the validation fixture adjacent inside the EOS repository.
rulings.reason: It has no independent life, owner, remote or handover boundary, so option C applies.

rulings.decision: Use filesystem and egress containment as the floor, with a configuration rule that prevents private data, untrusted content and outbound communication from coexisting. Treat in-band detection only as a tripwire.
rulings.reason: The task class is not proven plannable and no deterministic monitor is validated, so option B on top of D is the safe rule.

rulings.decision: Require a staged pre-commit secret scan and a push-path scan before this agent-written repository may hold credentials.
rulings.reason: Agents can commit and the GitHub path is public-adjacent, so options B and C must be used together. The ruling sets an admission condition rather than claiming those controls are already installed.

rulings.decision: Use option C: apply ASVS level 1 as the entry bar, require level 2 only if the surface starts holding personal data, money or another party's credentials, and record exclusions per surface.
rulings.reason: The committed fixture may persist beyond a quarter, while its current data sensitivity requires level 1 rather than level 2.

rulings.decision: Classify consequential actions through option C and fall closed to option D: the agent proposes and the operator executes manually until a validated enforcement adapter exists.
rulings.reason: The declared guard adapter is manual and unvalidated, which the decision rule treats as a valid fail-closed working state.

rulings.decision: Split only the independently owned boundary and retain the remaining system as one deployable.
rulings.reason: The named boundary must release independently; no other boundary has earned distribution.

departures.reason: Independent release ownership requires one scoped exception to the one-deployable default.
